Why are wallet transactions marked as Credit?

Wallet transactions (Amazon Pay, Paytm, etc.) are marked as Credit because they\'re charged to your bank account or credit card first, not direct bank debits. This helps track the actual payment method used.
What\'s the difference between the 5 transaction types?

• Expense: Money going out of your account (debits, purchases, bill payments)
• Income: Money coming into your account (salary, refunds, cashback)
• Investment: Mutual funds, stocks, SIPs, trading accounts
• Credit: Credit card transactions and wallet payments (money you'll pay later)
• Transfer: Money moved between your own accounts (self-transfers)
When should I use Transfer vs Expense?

Use Transfer when moving money between your own accounts (e.g., savings to checking). These don\'t affect your net worth. Use Expense for actual spending.\n\nPaired transfers from SMS are detected automatically: a merchantless debit and an equal credit on another of your accounts minutes apart become one Transfer, so moving money between your accounts never reads as spending.
Someone sent me money that I\'ll pass on to someone else. How do I record it?

Don\'t leave it as income — it would overstate what you earned. Open the transaction and set its type to Transfer (long-pressing the row in the list offers the same shortcut); transfers stay out of both income and spending. If the money isn\'t moving between your own accounts — you\'re simply holding it for someone — turn on \"Exclude from analytics\" instead: the row stays in your history and keeps the account balance honest, but stops counting in income, spending, budgets and insights.
I paid for something a friend will pay me back for. How should I record it?

Record the payment as the expense it was, then mark it as a loan: open the transaction, choose \"Mark as loan\", pick Lent and enter their name. Loan-linked rows are kept out of your category spending and budgets, and the Loans screen tracks what is still owed. When they pay you back, record the repayment against that loan rather than as ordinary income. Until it is repaid the outstanding amount still shows as money out on the Home card — you haven\'t got it back yet.
How do I stop a single transaction from affecting my totals?

Open it and switch on \"Exclude from analytics\". The row keeps its place in your history, still updates the account balance and is marked as excluded in the list — it simply stops counting in income, spending, budgets, insights and the widgets. That\'s the right switch for money that passes through your account without being yours: pass-through amounts, reimbursements, a mis-detected SMS.
Why aren\'t my bank SMS being detected?
Check if your bank is supported in our list. If not, report it via GitHub. Ensure SMS permissions are granted and the sender format matches standard bank SMS patterns.
They\'re saved in \'Unrecognized Messages\' where you can manually review them or report them to help us improve parsing.
Some banks send multiple SMS for the same transaction. The app tries to detect duplicates, but you can manually delete any that slip through.
Yes! All data stays on your device. We don\'t have servers or cloud storage.
Currently, data is stored locally only. Export/backup features are planned for future updates.
What data does the app access?
Only SMS messages from known bank senders. We don\'t read personal messages or access other app data.
Manual accounts let you track cash, investments, or accounts from unsupported banks. You update balances manually.
How do I track multiple accounts from the same bank?

The app automatically detects different accounts based on the last 4 digits shown in SMS. Each account keeps its own balance and currency; the account filter on the Transactions screen views them separately, and \"All accounts\" combines them. Profile switching (Personal / Business) sits separately from accounts.
How do I hide an account I don\'t want to see?

Settings → Manage Accounts, then the ⋮ menu on the account and Hide. It moves to the hidden accounts section and drops out of balances and filters; its transactions and history are untouched, and Show brings it straight back. Same menu for cards.
Can I hide or rename the built-in categories?

Any category can be hidden — the eye icon on its row takes it out of the pickers while its transactions keep the label. Built-in categories can\'t be renamed or deleted, because SMS categorisation and rules match them by name: renaming one would quietly stop it matching. For your own groupings, add a custom category instead.
